errors.validation_error: Some of the values are not valid. Check the form and try again.
errors.unauthorized: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
errors.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.
errors.internal_error: Something went wrong on the server.
errors.not_initialized: Mewte has not been set up yet.
errors.already_initialized: Mewte has already been set up. Sign in instead.
errors.totp_required: Enter your two-factor code to continue.
errors.totp_invalid: That code is incorrect or has already been used.
errors.totp_not_pending: Two-factor authentication is not set up.
errors.github_token_invalid: GitHub rejected this token. Check that it was copied in full and has not expired.
errors.github_token_missing_scope: This token cannot read notifications. Use a classic personal access token with the notifications scope.
errors.github_unreachable: Could not reach GitHub. Try again in a moment.
errors.account_exists: This GitHub account is already connected.
errors.account_mismatch: This token belongs to a different GitHub account.
errors.account_busy: This account is already running. Try again when it finishes.

setup.title: Welcome to Mewte
setup.description: Create the owner account. Mewte has a single user, so this is the only account there will be.
setup.usernameHint: Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore.
setup.passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match.
setup.setupTokenHint: The value of the SETUP_TOKEN environment variable on the server.

login.title: Sign in to Mewte
login.codeDescription: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
login.recoveryDescription: Enter one of your recovery codes. Each code works once.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.chartDescription: Per day over the last 14 days
dashboard.noRunsDescription: Runs appear here once an account has been polled.
dashboard.getStartedDescription: Connect a GitHub account, then add a rule that says which notifications to clear.

accounts.title: GitHub accounts
accounts.description: Mewte polls the notifications of each connected account on its own schedule.
accounts.emptyDescription: Connect a GitHub account with a personal access token to start clearing its notifications.
accounts.unauthorizedHint: GitHub no longer accepts this token, so polling has stopped. Replace the token to resume.
accounts.intervalHint: How often to check for notifications. The minimum is 1 minute. GitHub may ask for a longer wait, which is always respected.
accounts.noRepoScope: Without the repo scope, rules cannot read the author, labels, state, reviewers or comments of private repositories.
accounts.verified: Token checked, scopes are up to date
accounts.noRules: No enabled rule applies to this account, so its notifications are only counted.
accounts.runSummary: Checked {{fetched}} notifications: {{matched}} matched a rule, {{processed}} marked as done.
accounts.runNoRules: {{fetched}} notifications are waiting, but no enabled rule applies to this account, so none was marked as done.
accounts.backlogDescription: Mewte leaves alone the notifications that were already read when it started watching this account. This checks every notification GitHub still lists for the account against the rules, once, and marks the matches as done. It cannot be undone and may take a few minutes. GitHub also lists notifications you marked as done yourself, so those can show up in the history too. If GitHub's rate limit interrupts it, run it again.
accounts.replaceTokenHint: Leave empty to keep the current token. A new token must belong to the same GitHub account.
accounts.deleteDescription: The stored token is deleted and polling stops. History and run logs are kept.
accounts.addDescription: Mewte needs a classic personal access token. Fine-grained tokens and GitHub App tokens cannot read notifications.
accounts.tokenStorage: The token is encrypted before it is stored and is never shown again.
accounts.howToStep1: Open GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic).
accounts.howToStep2: Generate a new classic token and select the notifications scope.
accounts.howToStep3: Also select repo if rules should match on the author, labels, state, reviewers or comments of private repositories.
accounts.howToStep4: Copy the token and paste it here.
accounts.openTokenPage: Open the token page on GitHub

rules.title: Rules
rules.description: Each notification is checked against the rules from top to bottom. The first rule that matches wins.
rules.emptyDescription: A rule describes which notifications should be marked as done.
rules.name: Name
rules.actionHint: GitHub cannot undo this. The notification leaves your inbox for good.
rules.conditionHint: A condition that needs data GitHub will not provide for a notification, such as the state of a release, never matches.
rules.deleteDescription: The rule stops applying immediately. History entries it created are kept.
rules.invalid: Fill in every condition before saving.
rules.previewDescription: See which of your current notifications this rule would mark as done. Nothing is changed.
rules.previewUndecided: {{count}} could not be decided, because GitHub did not return the details this rule needs:
rules.previewUndecidedPrivate: Private repository: the token lacks the repo scope.
rules.previewUndecidedOther: GitHub did not return these details.
rules.previewBacklogHint: Notifications that were already read when Mewte started watching the account are not included. To handle them, use "Clear read backlog" on the account.
rules.fileSynced: Rules are mirrored in {{path}}. Editing that file changes the rules, and saving a rule here rewrites the file.
rules.fileInvalidHint: The edits in {{path}} were not applied. The rules below are the last valid ones.

conditions.groupOperator: How to combine the conditions in this group
conditions.valuesPlaceholder: Type a value and press Enter
conditions.patternHint: Use * as a wildcard. Matching ignores case.
conditions.emptyGroup: This group has no conditions yet.

fieldHints.repo: Full name, such as owner/name or owner/*.
fieldHints.owner: The user or organization that owns the repository.
fieldHints.actor: Whoever wrote the latest comment, or the author when there is none.
fieldHints.reviewer: People asked to review plus people who have reviewed.
fieldHints.commenter: Everyone who has commented, including review comments.
fieldHints.state: Issues are open or closed. Pull requests can also be merged or draft, and discussions answered.

conditions.invalidRegex: This is not a valid regular expression.

history.title: History
history.description: A snapshot of every notification a rule has cleared. GitHub cannot restore a notification that was marked as done, so each entry links back to its subject instead.
history.emptyDescription: Notifications appear here after a rule marks them as done.

runs.title: Run logs
runs.description: One entry for every time an account was polled.
runs.emptyDescription: Runs appear here once an account has been polled.

settings.title: Settings
settings.retentionDescription: History and run logs older than this are deleted by an hourly job.
settings.appearanceDescription: These preferences are saved in this browser.
settings.passwordDescription: Changing the password signs out every other session.

totp.title: Two-factor authentication
totp.description: Ask for a code from an authenticator app at sign-in, in addition to the password.
totp.setupStep1: Scan this QR code with an authenticator app.
totp.qrLabel: QR code for the authenticator app
totp.manualEntry: Or enter this key by hand:
totp.setupStep2: Enter the 6-digit code the app shows to confirm.
totp.recoveryDescription: Each code signs you in once if you lose your authenticator. They are shown only now, so store them somewhere safe.
totp.disableDescription: Sign-in will ask for the password only. Enter your password to confirm.
totp.regenerateDescription: The current recovery codes stop working. Enter your password to confirm.
